menu_options.pick_device: Set up a charger over Bluetooth (recommended)
menu_options.manual: The charger is already on the network — enter its number

bluetooth_confirm.title: GNLT charger nearby
bluetooth_confirm.description: Home Assistant sees the charger {name} over Bluetooth. Set it up: Home Assistant will write your Wi-Fi network and its own address into the charger.

pick_device.title: Choose the charger
pick_device.description: The charger is visible over Bluetooth only while OCPP is switched off on it: on the charger screen open Settings → Wi-Fi and switch OCPP off. Keep the Home Assistant Bluetooth adapter (or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy) within a few metres of the charger.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi for the charger
wifi.description: The charger {name} will join this network and connect to Home Assistant. The network must be 2.4 GHz; the name and password may contain Latin letters, digits and symbols only. The password is sent to the charger and is not stored in Home Assistant.

data.host: Home Assistant address in your network
data.plug_and_charge_off: Start charging by command, not by plugging in

data_description.host: The charger connects to this address. Usually detected automatically — check that it is the address of Home Assistant in your home network.
data_description.port: The same port for all chargers. Do not open it to the internet.
data_description.plug_and_charge_off: Recommended. Then every charge is visible and controllable in Home Assistant. To start charging automatically when the cable is plugged in, use the "Start when the cable is connected" switch.

passport.title: Charger version
passport.description: Charger {serial} is set up. Check its version: it limits the current slider. If the charger reported it itself, it is already selected.

enable_ocpp.title: Last step — on the charger
enable_ocpp.description:
1. Wait until the Wi-Fi icon appears on the charger screen — this means the network name and password were accepted.
2. Then open Settings → Wi-Fi on the charger and switch OCPP on.

This step is done by hand, on the charger itself. Press "Submit" when OCPP is on — Home Assistant will wait for charger {serial} to connect.

not_connected.title: The charger has not connected yet

manual_address.title: Enter the address in the charger
manual_address.description:
In the OCPP settings of the charger enter:

- server address: `{url}`
- ChargeID: `{serial}`

The address starts with **ws://**, not wss://. Then switch OCPP on in Settings → Wi-Fi on the charger. If Home Assistant runs in Docker without host networking, this address may be the container's own - then enter the address of the computer in your home network (or set it in Settings → System → Network → Local network).

discovery_confirm.title: Charger {serial} connected
discovery_confirm.description: Charger {serial} connected to Home Assistant. Choose its version to add it.

progress.provision: Writing the settings into the charger over Bluetooth. Stay close to the charger, it takes about half a minute.
progress.wait_connect: Waiting for the charger to connect to Home Assistant (up to 10 minutes).

error.no_devices: No charger found over Bluetooth. Switch OCPP off on the charger (Settings → Wi-Fi) and try again.
error.ssid_ascii: The charger accepts only Latin letters, digits and symbols in the network name. Rename the network in the router settings.
error.ssid_long: Network name is longer than 32 characters.
error.password_ascii: The charger accepts only Latin letters, digits and symbols in the password.
error.host_ascii: The address may contain Latin letters, digits and symbols only.
error.host_long: The address is too long for the charger (128 characters at most).
error.host_empty: Enter the address of Home Assistant.
error.port_busy: This port is taken by another program. Choose another one.
error.serial_invalid: The serial number consists of 12 digits.
error.ble_not_found: The charger is out of Bluetooth range. Move closer or add an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy near it.
error.ble_connect_failed: Could not connect to the charger over Bluetooth. Check that OCPP is switched off on it and try again.
error.ble_not_charger: This device does not answer like a GNLT charger.
error.ble_no_answer: The charger stopped answering. Move closer and try again.
error.ble_rejected: The charger did not accept the settings. Check the network name and password.
error.ble_failed: Setup over Bluetooth failed. Try again.
error.firmware_too_old: This charger version cannot work with Home Assistant over OCPP. Contact the seller.

abort.already_in_progress: This charger is already being set up.
abort.not_supported: This device is not a GNLT charger.
abort.reprovisioned: The charger received the new network settings. Switch OCPP on in Settings → Wi-Fi on the charger — it will reconnect to Home Assistant.

init.title: Charger settings

data.auto_start: Start when the cable is connected
data.resume_after_power_loss: Continue charging after a power cut
data.meter_interval: How often the charger sends readings, seconds

data_description.auto_start: Home Assistant starts the charge itself when you plug the cable into the car. Cannot be combined with the schedule: turning one on turns the other off.
data_description.resume_after_power_loss: If the power went out during a charge, Home Assistant continues it when the power returns — as long as the cable was not unplugged. Works on chargers version 2.8 and newer.
data_description.price: Used to calculate the cost of every charge. Empty or 0 - cost is not calculated.
data_description.night_price: For a two-zone tariff. 0 means a single tariff. Energy delivered at night is priced at this rate even if the charge started in the day.

init.description: Prices are per 1 kWh, in the currency of Home Assistant ({currency}).

state.evcommunicationerror: Charger and car did not agree

charging_without_session.name: Charging started by the charger itself

empty_session.name: The car did not start charging

auto_start.name: Start when the cable is connected

schedule_stop_at_end.name: Stop at the end of the schedule

not_connected.message: The charger is not connected to Home Assistant.

no_answer.message: The charger did not answer in time. Try again.

call_error.message: The charger could not process the command ({detail}).

rejected.message: The charger did not accept the command ({detail}).

current_out_of_range.message: The current must be within {detail} A.

unavailable.message: The charger is out of service now.

no_session.message: This charge was started by the charger itself and cannot be stopped with the usual command. Use the "Interrupt charging" button or unplug the cable.

nothing_to_interrupt.message: Nothing to interrupt: the charger is not charging by itself right now. To stop a normal charge, use the "Charging" switch.

not_supported.message: This charger does not support this setting over OCPP.

replug.message: The car did not take current last time, and the charger will not accept a new start. Unplug the cable, plug it in again and start.
